summary: Steel fire tower near Elba, Minnesota, retired in the early 1960s, restored and reopened to visitors in 1997; now run by state parks.

facts.design: 110-foot tower with a 7-by-7-foot cab (Register and 1936 report); a 1973 survey note describes steel construction, about 130 feet

access.note: DNR lists daylight hours April through October (page undated). A 1997 article gave 5 a.m. to 10 p.m. daily. Check current hours.

visit.trail_note: About 500 uneven steps (DNR) or 634 steps (1997 article) from the parking lot off Winona 26 east of Elba up the bluff to the tower.

events.note: Register says the CCC constructed it in 1936; a 1936 press report says it had been erected. DNR and a 1997 article say 1933.
George Meyers, superintendent of the Whitewater Game Refuge, is reported to have manned the tower.
Peter Kronebusch named as towerman; tower manned when fire hazard was present.
Post-Bulletin article dated June 26, 1997 announced the restored tower would reopen to visitors after a dedication ceremony Saturday.

notes_for_editor: Built year conflicts: the Register and a 1936 press report say 1936 (CCC); the DNR page and a 1997 Post-Bulletin article say 1933. Not resolved. Height conflicts: Register and 1936 report say 110 ft (33.5 m, used in facts); 1997 article says 100 ft; a 1973 NGS description says about 130 ft; the OSM node tag says 35 m (the current record value). Steps conflict: DNR says about 500, 1997 article says 634. Hours conflict: DNR gives daylight hours April to October (page undated); 1997 article gave 5 a.m. to 10 p.m. Current access and condition not confirmed by any dated source after 1997 except the undated DNR page; check before publishing visit details. Record access 'unknown' can be set to public per DNR. No photos added; NHLR and Post-Bulletin pages were not checked for licensed images.
